title: Convergence agreement for scope tradeoffs and legal obligations for privacy-locked rollout
creator: Priya Nair
description: Create and land a single-source 'convergence agreement' document that captures final scope tradeoffs, legally required obligations, and explicit acceptance criteria for the privacy-locked (regional data residency) rollout of Private Edition. This ticket coordinates the cross-team signoff workstream (Engineering, Design, Legal, Security) so the PRD can proceed to implementation without late-stage surprises.
context: PM published initial PRD v0.9 on 2026-02-15 describing regional storage, audit logs, and optional on-prem agents. Engineering surfaced three scope options (A/B/C) with different cost and latency profiles. Legal listed mandatory contract language for data residency and auditability. Design produced a condensed UX flow but flagged consent language flows for localized markets. Multiple teams requested a canonical acceptance matrix to avoid rework during the rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Legal approval: signed checklist confirming required contract clauses, export-control stub, and data residency template (link to legal doc).
Design approval: final UX mocks for consent and admin console flows, responsive states, and edge-case microcopy revisions reviewed and approved by Design Lead.

Engineering acceptance: performance SLOs defined for regional mode (P95 latency <= 220ms for synthetic test), migration script for customer data verified in staging, and runbook for rollback appended.
Security verification: KMS integration validated end-to-end in staging and audit logs proof-of-concept ingested into observability pipeline.
Operational readiness: capacity reservation plan for Dedicated pools and a fallback routing policy documented in Console runbook.
Signed convergence doc: representatives from PM, Eng, Design, Legal, and Security have added explicit approval entries and agreed to the chosen scope variant (A/B/C).
decisions: Choose Scope Variant B (regional storage + optional on-prem agent) as default for GA; Variant C (full on-prem) staged as enterprise add-on. Decision driven by customer impact and implementation velocity.
Require Legal to provide a single redlineable clause template for data residency and export controls; contract must be attachable to onboarding flow.
Design will standardize consent copy across EU/APAC; localization owners to provide translations before signoff.
Engineering will target a canary rollout with 10% traffic and automated rollback hooks before broad enablement.
tradeoffs: Scope B increases storage costs (~12%) because of regional duplication but reduces regulatory risk and accelerates sales conversations in EU markets.
Delaying Variant C (on‑prem) reduces legal/compliance burden at GA but requires a dedicated roadmap line for enterprise integrations, potentially lengthening sales cycles for those accounts.
Tight SLO targets require additional caching engineering work which increases short-term dev effort but reduces long-term cost per token.
timeline: Key milestones: 2026-03-03 cross-team workshop; 2026-03-10 convergence doc draft; 2026-03-18 legal signoff; 2026-03-22 design handoff; 2026-03-25 golden path verification and final approvals. Target GA enablement window is 2026-04-05 to 2026-04-12 depending on canary results.
comments: 2026-03-03: Cross-team workshop summary — Eng presented perf delta matrix for Scope A/B/C; Legal flagged international transfer language; Design proposed motion to collapse two consent screens into one. (author: Leo Martinez)
2026-03-05: PM updated acceptance matrix to include KMS verification steps and a staging checklist for data migration. Requested Legal provide redlines by 2026-03-10. (author: Priya Nair)

2026-03-08: Legal returned initial redline; flagged need for clause for customer-managed keys; added requirement for retention policy disclosure. Action: Security to validate KMS modes. (author: Marta Kuznetsova)
2026-03-09: Design reviewed copy updates and uploaded v3 mocks. Small UX change agreed — show region selector earlier in onboarding flow. (author: Diego Alvarez)
2026-03-10: Engineering canary plan created (GH PR #128). Added perf test harness and migration dry-run. Requesting one more day for runbook writeup. (author: Anika Patel)
qa_plan: QA will run a two-stage verification: (1) staging smoke tests for regional storage and audit logs (pass criteria: no loss and correct residency tags), (2) canary traffic validation with synthetic workload comparing latency and error rate against baseline. All failures to be triaged within 4 hours during the canary window.
rollout_plan: Phased rollout: Internal beta (10 orgs) -> external canary (10% traffic) -> ramp by 25% increments monitoring key telemetry. Rollback criteria: >3x error rate increase or sustained P95 latency regression >2x baseline for 30 minutes. Communications: Customer success notified at each ramp; legal and security on-call during canary.
